name: cropper

frames.best_why: Photo fills the rounded frame with the white crop square centred and the dimmed surround clearly visible.

tagline: Drag and zoom a photo behind a fixed white square frame.
summary: An image cropper: a photo sits in a rounded frame with a fixed square outline and everything outside it dimmed. Dragging moves the picture beneath the square and scrolling or pinching zooms it.
appearance: A photograph of mountains above clouds inside a rounded rectangle about 16 by 10. A thin white square outline sits centrally with everything outside it darkened, and a small grey instruction line runs underneath.
behaviour: Dragging pans the photo beneath the stationary crop square, while scrolling or pinching zooms it between set limits. The white square never changes size; only the image moves and scales.
demo_content: A snow-capped mountain range over a sea of clouds at sunset, captioned 'Drag to reposition · Scroll to zoom'.
search_phrases: drag a square over a photo
white frame to choose a picture area
pinch to zoom an upload preview
use_when: A user must choose the visible part of a photo before it is saved or uploaded.
avoid_when: The crop is always a square with no ratio control, and it needs a real image URL to show anything.
customise: The image URL and zoom limits are props; the crop square, dimmed overlay and frame styling are changed through classes on the four sub-parts.
weight_why: One large image with pointer-driven transforms; nothing loops until the user drags.

a11y.note: Dragging and scrolling are the only controls, so keyboard users cannot pan or zoom; a hidden description is supplied for screen readers.

issues: The crop is always square; no aspect ratio is offered
The instruction caption below the image is very small and low contrast
polish_why: Clean photo and a clear white crop edge; no ratio control and the hint text is tiny.
title: Image Cropper
